title: Equal parts need not look alike

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This whole rectangle has twenty four little squares in four colored parts.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: They aren't equal. They look different!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's check the space they cover. That space is called area. These little squares are all the same size.

do.meaning: How much flat space a shape covers.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Count the strip's squares. One, two, three, four, five, six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The block has three squares in each row. Three and three make six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The bent part: one, two, three, four, five, six.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: And the long corner has five along the bottom, and one above. Six too!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Watch what happens when we rearrange the squares.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The strip becomes a block: two across, three down.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The next part slides into exactly the same shape.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The long corner fits too. No squares added. None taken away.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And the bent part settles into the same six spaces.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: All four blocks match! So all four parts have equal area.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Send every square home. Their outlines change. Their areas do not.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four parts with equal area fill this whole rectangle.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each part is one fourth of the whole area.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The bottom number counts the equal parts in the whole. The top number says we mean one of them.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Even the long, skinny part is one fourth.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keep the whole rectangle the same. Share its twenty four squares three ways.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Eight squares in each of three equal parts. Each is one third.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Split each part in two. Six equal parts, four squares each. Each is one sixth.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Or share the whole eight ways. Three squares each: one eighth.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: More equal parts of the same whole means less area in each!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What about this rectangle? Four pieces again. Are they all fourths?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: I need to check their areas.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four squares, six, six, and eight. These pieces do not share the area equally.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A fourth of twenty four is six. The two six-square pieces are fourths. The four-square piece is smaller; the eight-square piece is larger.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Four pieces doesn't mean four equal shares.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Return to our four equal parts. Suppose each little square is one square unit.

do.text: Find the area of one part

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The whole area is twenty four square units. Share it equally among four parts.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Six square units in each part.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Check: four groups of six give twenty four. One fourth tells the share of the whole. Six square units tells its area.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try a different whole: thirty square units, split into five equal parts. What is one part's area?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Thirty divided by five. Six square units.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Yes. Five sixes make thirty. Here, six square units is one fifth of the whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two copies of the same rectangle. A straight cut makes two parts of twelve squares.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The stepped cut also leaves twelve squares on each side. Two equal areas, so each part is one half.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: A half doesn't need a straight cut. It needs half the area.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Different outlines. Six squares in every part. Each is one fourth of this whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Equal parts have equal area. Count the equal parts to name the fraction.
